public.label: 01 / Public climate investment
public.title: Investing in warning systems that avert future losses.
public.desc: Early warning systems create social benefits, but investment approval needs defensible avoided-loss estimates, long-term operating finance and clear institutional ownership.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Benefits and avoided losses hard to value
public.note: Economic benefits can include avoided harm and losses, but they do not automatically generate cash for annual operating expenses. Fiscal and institutional sustainability require separate appraisal.

private.label: 01 / Private resilience investment
private.title: Should a logistics company invest in business-continuity infrastructure?
private.desc: Flood protection, resilient storage and redundant systems may reduce downtime. The investor must separate true incremental savings from overly optimistic assumptions.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: An exposure not priced into capex
problems: Uncertain frequency and cost of disruption
Insurance, repairs and downtime tracked separately
private.note: Commercial benefits in this hypothetical case are annual avoided losses and operating gains. Validate probabilities, timing, financing costs and residual risk before committing capital.

public.label: 02 / Human-capital investment
public.title: Can education infrastructure generate lasting social returns?
public.desc: Education investments need to link learning, retention and future productivity gains to credible costs while testing whether institutions can operate and maintain new services.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Learning gains are long-dated and uncertain
Capex and recurrent budgets evaluated separately
Weak links between costs, inclusion and benefits
public.note: Human-capital benefit streams depend on causal learning effects, counterfactual outcomes and earnings assumptions. The demonstration uses simplified equal annual economic benefit flows—not a real education-project model.

private.label: 02 / Private skills investment
private.title: When does a new workforce academy earn back its investment?
private.desc: A firm planning an in-house skills facility must connect training expenditure to measurable productivity, retention and quality improvements rather than enrolment counts alone.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: Training budget mistaken for an outcome
problems: Training and attrition costs left out
private.note: Productivity and retention gains are hypothetical cash-equivalent benefits here; they would require direct measurement and conservative attribution in a real corporate decision.

public.label: 03 / Green public investment
public.title: Designing an energy transition that can be financed and maintained.
public.desc: Green infrastructure policy requires a connection between emissions, environmental benefits, service reliability, funding needs and the ability of agencies to execute.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Projects not screened by value and readiness
Benefits, tariffs and fiscal costs conflated
public.note: Economic returns on a public green project differ from tariff revenue and fiscal funding. Carbon prices, shadow pricing and externalities would require project-specific evidence.

private.label: 03 / Factory efficiency investment
private.title: Does an energy-efficient motor upgrade make commercial sense?
private.desc: A manufacturing firm needs to consider equipment cost, energy savings, utilisation, maintenance, credit constraints and workers’ willingness to adopt new technology.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.note: This is a hypothetical technology-adoption investment application. The equipment investment numbers and finance workflow shown here are invented examples, not observed returns.

public.label: 04 / Public capital programme
public.title: Turning an infrastructure wish-list into a financeable investment pipeline.
public.desc: Local infrastructure can promise development gains yet stall because of weak project screening, unclear repayment capacity, fragmented approvals and operating cost gaps.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Projects ranked without shared appraisal rules
Cost overruns and procurement risk overlooked
public.note: The economic-NPV illustration is not a debt-service forecast or municipal-budget cash flow. Public investment selection also requires fiscal affordability, distributional review and governance.

private.label: 04 / Enterprise growth investment
private.title: How much expansion capital should an enterprise actually commit?
private.desc: When demand forecasts, financing costs and execution capacity are uncertain, expansion is a sequence of capital-allocation decisions—not a single optimistic sales projection.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
outputs: Milestones for pilot, expand or defer
private.note: The model reports project financial returns from hypothetical cash flows before financing and tax complications. Actual enterprise investment needs detailed operating, tax and debt schedules.
